chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shaza'an, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a slave girl whom he would sleep with, and news reached him that she had a husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He can sleep with her, for her sale is her divorce, and that is because they are both unable to do anything regarding their matter when she is sold.'

key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: he sleeps with her / consummates marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man sleeping with a slave girl he bought if she already has a husband?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the mechanism of *tamlik al-zawj* (acquiring the husband) in the context of slave marriage, ruling that the sale of the wife to a new master constitutes an immediate, irrevocable divorce (*talaq*) from her previous husband. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of slave marriages in Shia jurisprudence, where the husband's consent is not required for separation, ensuring the slave woman is free to be consummated by her new owner without waiting for a period. The narration underscores the practical reality that since neither party can easily reclaim the other, the sale serves as a definitive severance of the marital bond.
